questions.question: Which description fits the **PlanDefinition** resource?
options: This resource allows for the definition of various types of plans as a sharable, consumable, and executable artifact.
A structured set of questions intended to guide the collection of answers from end-users.
This resource provides a reusable description of when a particular event can occur.
A kind of specimen with associated set of requirements.
questions.explanation: **PlanDefinition**: This resource allows for the definition of various types of plans as a sharable, consumable, and executable artifact. The resource is general enough to support the description of a broad range of clinical artifacts such as clinical decision support rules, order sets and protocols. The other descriptions belong to **Questionnaire**, **EventDefinition**, **SpecimenDefinition**.

questions.question: Which resource would you use? A reusable sepsis protocol listing the actions to take and when.
questions.explanation: **PlanDefinition**. A definition (template) of a plan, applied to a patient to create a CarePlan or RequestGroup.

questions.question: You know **PlanDefinition**. Which resource should you use instead when you need “one activity, not a whole plan”?
questions.explanation: **ActivityDefinition**: one activity, not a whole plan. **PlanDefinition** is for something else: This resource allows for the definition of various types of plans as a sharable, consumable, and executable artifact.

questions.question: Which element is **required** (minimum cardinality 1) in every **PlanDefinition** instance?
questions.explanation: The required top-level elements of PlanDefinition are `status` (1..1). The other options have a minimum cardinality of 0, so they are optional.

questions.question: Which element of **PlanDefinition** is a **modifier** (?!), so receiving systems must not ignore it?
questions.explanation: Modifier elements of PlanDefinition: `status`. `status`: draft | active | retired | unknown. A modifier can change the meaning of the whole resource: for example, a status of `entered-in-error` means the data must not be used.
